This is NOT a description of the API surface - that is DERIVED by
This file is an exception log: each entry is a decision that a key may
vanish, plus the reason it is safe.
Adding an entry here is the LAST resort. Prefer keeping the old key
alongside the new one (a compatibility alias) - additive change is never
blocked by this guard, so serving both costs nothing.
After adding an entry, regenerate the baseline:

_entry_shape.endpoint: GET /api/example  (METHOD + path, exactly as it appears in api_response_surface.json)
_entry_shape.reason: why this removal is safe - who was reading it and what they read now

allowed_removals.reason: It counted the population behind the /sites/<id> sitemap block removed in #4436 (the facilities table has no updated_at column, so that block raised on every build and emitted zero URLs; the pages are robots-blocked besides). The count described that block and nothing else the generator emits. Its only reader was GET /api/v1/status's sitemap block, which drops the mirrored key in this same PR rather than publishing a null; no reader in dchub-frontend or dchub-mcp-server (grepped both).

These keys were NEVER SERVED. The path had two registrations and the contract merges both; these come only from the capacity_headroom_api.py copy, which never matched a request — routes/energy_discovery_routes registers the same rule earlier (main.py ~36380 vs ~40590) and Flask matches the first, verified by booting the app and reading url_map. The live handler's keys (success, markets, count, _gated, _required_tier, _upgrade_cta) are all unchanged. No consumer read the removed keys: dchub-frontend/js/capacity-heatmap-layer.js reads data.markets and contains no 'legend' or 'points' reference at all (the guard's 'read by' hit on legend.F.label was the bare token 'label' in m.readiness.label). The dead copy was removed because it carried @require_plan('pro') with NO in-body redaction while the copy that wins HAS one, so a registration-order change would have silently promoted an UNGATED twin of a gated route into service.

routes/email_engagement.py deleted 2026-08-28. Its webhook twin was shadowed by resend_webhook (Flask serves the FIRST registration), so the email_engagement table had 0 rows all-time and this endpoint served {count:0,events:[]} forever. No consumer in dchub-frontend or dchub-mcp-server; delivery truth lives in email_events via GET /api/v1/admin/email-events.

'recorded_id' was a PHANTOM key: only the SHADOWED email_engagement.resend_webhook returned it. The live handler (resend_webhook.resend_webhook) has only ever returned {ok:true}, so no caller could observe recorded_id. Removed with the shadowed blueprint.

Removed 2026-09-11 (seo_agent.py): the route had no auth gate, so any anonymous caller could make it submit URLs to IndexNow under our key. Nothing read its response: Railway counted no requests in the 7 days before removal, and no file in dchub-backend, dchub-frontend or dchub-mcp-server names the path. Submits go through the admin-gated POST /api/v1/admin/indexnow.

Removed 2026-09-11 (seo_agent.py) with POST /api/seo/indexnow/ping-all: the same ungated IndexNow submit, bundled with two reads. No requests in the 7 days before removal (Railway), and no file in the three repos names the path. Both reads are still served on their own, at GET /api/seo/content-ideas and GET /api/seo/ai-citations.
